access.edition_or_version: The Complete Works of Zhuangzi, trans. Burton Watson (Columbia University Press, 2013)

mechanics.premise: Perspective, naturalness and the limits of knowledge explored through argument, story and paradox.
mechanics.argumentative_stance: Indirect: a tale or paradox is made to carry the abstract point rather than an explicit thesis defended.
mechanics.point_of_view: Shifting voices; dialogues between masters, craftsmen and creatures.
mechanics.structure: Chapter-level theme built from loosely joined anecdotes and dialogues rather than continuous argument.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Parable, thought-experiment, reductio, pun and paradox; the 'Butterfly Dream' turns on the dream/waking distinction.
mechanics.dialogue: Teaching exchanges in which a master answers a question with an image or counter-question.
mechanics.imagery: Transformation imagery (butterfly, fish, tree, cook) that embodies claims about change and usefulness.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Perplexity opening toward equanimity and release from fixed categories.
mechanics.critical_reception: Foundational Daoist text and a model of philosophical writing through narrative and paradox.
mechanics.failure_or_misuse_signals: Parable that only decorates, or paradox that only puzzles, without a recoverable idea, becomes whimsy.
